context.prd-excerpt:
Project: Link Shelf (slug: link-shelf). Greenfield, single repository, backend only. No template, no frontend, no container runtime. The target directory is already an initialised git repository: do NOT run `git init` and do NOT touch `.git`.
Feature: Save a link (slug: save-link, must-have). As someone collecting links, I want to store a URL with an optional title, so that I can come back to it without keeping a browser tab open. The URL is the only required field. If no title is supplied the field is stored as null rather than being derived from the page. Duplicate URLs are allowed.
Feature: List saved links (slug: list-links, must-have). As someone collecting links, I want to see what I have saved, newest first, so that I can find the thing I saved this morning without scrolling. A GET endpoint returning every saved link as a JSON array, newest first by created_at. No pagination.
Feature: Tag links (slug: tag-links, should-have). As someone collecting links, I want to tag what I save and filter by tag, so that a shelf of two hundred links stays usable. Attach zero or more free-text tags to a link, and filter the list endpoint by tag. Tags are a separate table with a many-to-many join to links.
Considerations (verbatim from tag-links): Tag names are matched case-sensitively. Case folding is a reasonable product decision but it is not free to verify, and leaving it explicit here stops an implementer inventing either behaviour and calling it correct.
CONSEQUENCES FOR THIS TASK: - This is the LAST task of the run. Layers 0, 1 and 2 are already merged, so every file they created EXISTS in this worktree. Nothing here is running in parallel with anything else. - Endpoint paths are UNPREFIXED: `/links` and `/links/{link_id}/tags`. The routers already carry those paths, so each is mounted with a bare `app.include_router(...)` and NO `prefix=` argument. Adding a prefix here would silently move every endpoint and break every path this task's test uses. - Tag names are CASE-SENSITIVE end to end. `?tag=Reading` must NOT match a tag stored as `reading`; it returns an empty array, not every link. - Do NOT implement orphan-tag cleanup. Whether a tag with no remaining links is deleted or kept is the tag-links OPEN GAP 1 (kind=decision, raised 2026-08-27): "Keeping them makes an autocomplete list easy and lets the list rot." No delete of any kind belongs in this task's output - no `db.delete`, no `cascade=`, no `ondelete=`, no orphan sweep, and no test that asserts either behaviour. Answering an undecided product question by accident is worse than leaving it open, because the accidental answer is invisible to whoever eventually decides it. - This task owns `app/main.py` and `tests/test_integration.py` and NOTHING else. Do not modify any Layer 2 router file, any schema, any model, or `tests/conftest.py`.

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI
@asynccontextmanager async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]: # startup work happens here yield # shutdown work would happen here
app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
This is FastAPI 0.110's supported startup hook. The decorated function receives the application instance, does its startup work, yields exactly once, and returns. Use it in preference to `@app.on_event("startup")`, which is deprecated in this FastAPI generation.

task.objective:
Mount the three existing routers - `save_link`, `list_links` and `tag_links` - on the existing FastAPI application in `app/main.py`, create the database schema at application startup so the file-backed application works when it is actually run and not only under test, and add `tests/test_integration.py`: an end-to-end test that saves two links, tags one of them, lists them unfiltered and lists them filtered by tag, all through the REAL mounted application.
That composition is the whole point of this task and no other task owns it. Every acceptance criterion of all three features is already satisfied and tested by Layer 2, and each Layer 2 test file proved its router correct against a throwaway application serving ONLY that router. None of them proved the three routers coexist: that they agree on one `LinkResponse` shape, that they share one database session through `get_db`, and that a link saved by one endpoint, tagged by a second, is found by the third.
This task therefore claims NO acceptance criterion - `satisfies-criteria` is empty on all three `source-feature` elements. Re-claiming a criterion Layer 2 already owns would make the coverage report ambiguous about which task actually proves it.

"""FastAPI application instance for Link Shelf."""
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI
import app.models # noqa: F401 - registers every model on Base.metadata from app.api.list_links import router as list_links_router from app.api.save_link import router as save_link_router from app.api.tag_links import router as tag_links_router from app.database import Base, engine, get_db
@asynccontextmanager async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]: """Create the file-backed schema before the application serves its first request.""" if get_db not in application.dependency_overrides: Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine) yield
app = FastAPI( title="Link Shelf", version="0.1.0", description="Store links with an optional title, list them newest first, and tag them.", lifespan=lifespan, )
app.include_router(save_link_router) app.include_router(list_links_router) app.include_router(tag_links_router)
Decisions embedded above that must be preserved exactly as written:
- The module-level name is still `app`, and `title`, `version` and `description` are unchanged. `tests/conftest.py` imports `from app.main import app as fastapi_app` and `tests/test_setup.py` asserts the OpenAPI title is `"Link Shelf"`; both must keep passing. The only change to the constructor call is the added `lifespan=lifespan` argument.
- THE THREE IMPORT LINES AND THE THREE ALIASES ARE EXACT. `save_link_router` from `app.api.save_link`, `list_links_router` from `app.api.list_links`, `tag_links_router` from `app.api.tag_links`. Each of those modules names its router `router` at module level; the alias is applied on import. Do not guess a different module path or a different name.
- `app.include_router(...)` is called with the router and NOTHING ELSE. Do NOT pass `prefix=`, `tags=`, `dependencies=` or `responses=`. Each router already carries its full unprefixed path - `/links` for two of them and `/links/{link_id}/tags` for the third - so a prefix here would move every endpoint and break every path in this task's test.
- All three routers are mounted. Mounting two of them and forgetting the third is the single most likely way this task fails silently: the missing endpoint answers 404 and the failure looks like a routing bug in somebody else's file.
- `POST /links` and `GET /links` share a path and differ by method; they do not conflict. `POST /links/{link_id}/tags` is a different path. Mount order does not affect routing here, but keep the order above so the file reads in the order the flow runs.
- `import app.models # noqa: F401` is deliberate and must stay. `Base.metadata.create_all` creates only the tables registered on the metadata, and they are registered by importing the model modules. The router imports happen to pull `app.models` in transitively, but relying on that would make the schema depend on an import three modules away. The `noqa` marks it as an intentionally unused import.
- `Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)` inside the lifespan is what makes the file-backed application work when it is actually run - `uvicorn app.main:app` against a fresh checkout would otherwise answer every request with "no such table: links". `create_all` issues `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, so it is a safe no-op on every subsequent start.
- `if get_db not in application.dependency_overrides:` is REQUIRED, not an optimisation. conftest's `client` fixture installs the `get_db` override BEFORE entering the TestClient, so during a test run the override is present and this branch is skipped. Without the guard, every test that uses the `client` fixture would open the FILE-BACKED engine and create `link_shelf.db` on disk - a database file that no test ever reads, written as a side effect of a test suite that is supposed to stay in memory. The guard states the rule exactly: if something has redirected `get_db`, this application is not using the file-backed engine and must not create its schema.
- Use `lifespan=`, NOT `@app.on_event("startup")`. The event decorator is deprecated in FastAPI 0.110 and emits a DeprecationWarning on import.
- Do NOT call `create_all` at module level. Import time is worse than startup time: merely importing `app.main` - which `tests/conftest.py` does at collection - would create the database file before any fixture had a chance to override anything.
- Do NOT define any route function in this file. The three routers own every endpoint. Do not add a `/health`, a `/` or a redirect: no criterion asks for one.
- Do NOT add a shutdown action after the `yield`. There is nothing to close - the engine's connections are pooled and disposed by the interpreter, and dropping tables at shutdown would destroy the caller's data.

Do NOT create or edit any other file. This task owns `app/main.py` and `tests/test_integration.py` and nothing else.
Specifically: do not touch `app/database.py`, `app/api/__init__.py`, `app/api/save_link.py`, `app/api/list_links.py`, `app/api/tag_links.py`, `app/schemas/link.py`, `app/schemas/tag.py`, any file under `app/models/`, `tests/conftest.py`, or any existing test file. If a Layer 2 router looks wrong, it is not wrong: it passed its own tests and its own verification, and editing it here would silently rewrite a task that has already been reviewed and merged.
Do not add `app/schemas/__init__.py` - `app/schemas` is a PEP 420 implicit namespace package and must stay one.
Do not create a migration - this project has no migration tool, the schema is created from `Base.metadata`. Do not run `git init` and do not touch `.git`.
Do NOT implement orphan-tag cleanup anywhere: no `db.delete(...)`, no `cascade=`, no `ondelete=`, no sweep of tags with no remaining links, and no test asserting that an orphaned tag is either kept or removed. That is the tag-links open gap 1 (kind=decision, raised 2026-08-27) and it must remain undecided.

titled = client.post( "/links", json={"url": "https://example.com/titled", "title": "The Titled One"}, ) assert titled.status_code == 201 titled_id = titled.json()["id"]
untitled = client.post("/links", json={"url": "https://example.com/untitled"}) assert untitled.status_code == 201 untitled_id = untitled.json()["id"] assert untitled.json()["title"] is None assert untitled_id != titled_id

by_id = {item["id"]: item for item in body} # the untitled link is REPORTED with a null title, not omitted from the listing assert "title" in by_id[untitled_id] assert by_id[untitled_id]["title"] is None assert by_id[untitled_id]["tags"] == [] assert by_id[titled_id]["title"] == "The Titled One" # the tag attached through the tagging endpoint survives the round trip through the # listing endpoint's response shape assert by_id[titled_id]["tags"] == ["reading"]
# GET /links?tag=: EXACTLY the tagged link filtered = client.get("/links", params={"tag": "reading"}) assert filtered.status_code == 200 filtered_body = filtered.json() assert [item["id"] for item in filtered_body] == [titled_id] assert filtered_body[0]["url"] == "https://example.com/titled" assert filtered_body[0]["tags"] == ["reading"]

A link written by `POST /links` being visible to `POST /links/{id}/tags` and then to `GET /links` is exactly the property being asserted.

Notes: - This is the "one LinkResponse" half of the composition. All three endpoints serialise through the single schema in `app/schemas/link.py`, so all three bodies must carry exactly the same five keys and report the same values for the same link. If a later change gave one endpoint its own response model, this test is what catches it. - `created_at` is compared as the raw ISO-8601 STRING across the POST and the GET. # app/main.py - the mounted application from collections.abc import AsyncIterator from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI
import app.models # noqa: F401 from app.api.list_links import router as list_links_router from app.api.save_link import router as save_link_router from app.api.tag_links import router as tag_links_router from app.database import Base, engine, get_db
@asynccontextmanager async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]: if get_db not in application.dependency_overrides: Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine) yield
app = FastAPI( title="Link Shelf", version="0.1.0", description="Store links with an optional title, list them newest first, and tag them.", lifespan=lifespan, )
app.include_router(save_link_router) app.include_router(list_links_router) app.include_router(tag_links_router)
Import as: `from app.main import app`. Run as: `uvicorn app.main:app`.
Downstream contract: - The application serves exactly three endpoints, all unprefixed: POST /links -> 201, a LinkResponse body GET /links[?tag=NAME] -> 200, a JSON array of LinkResponse, newest first POST /links/{link_id}/tags -> 200, a LinkResponse body with every attached tag No other route is defined here; FastAPI's own /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json remain. - All three serialise through the single `LinkResponse` schema in `app/schemas/link.py`, so every link body from every endpoint carries exactly `id, url, title, created_at, tags`. - All three take their session with `Depends(get_db)`, so overriding that one callable redirects the whole application at once. `tests/conftest.py`'s `client` fixture does exactly that, and it is now a fixture that serves real routes. - On startup the application creates the schema on the file-backed engine (`<repository root>/link_shelf.db`) with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, so a fresh checkout works on first run and an existing database is left alone. - Startup schema creation is SKIPPED when `get_db` is present in `app.dependency_overrides`, which is how the test suite runs entirely in memory and never writes `link_shelf.db`. Any future fixture that wraps this application must install its `get_db` override BEFORE entering the TestClient, or it will create the file. - Nothing is torn down at shutdown. The schema is never dropped. - The orphan-tag question (tag-links open gap 1, kind=decision, raised 2026-08-27) is still undecided. No part of this application deletes a tag or an attachment.

Downstream contract: - These are the ONLY tests in the project that exercise `app.main.app` with routes on it. Every Layer 2 test file mounts its own single router on a throwaway `FastAPI()` and therefore cannot detect a routing, prefix or schema disagreement between the three. - They claim NO acceptance criterion. All twelve criteria across the three features are owned and proved by L2-001, L2-002 and L2-003; these tests assert the composition, which no criterion states on its own. - What they will catch: a router mounted with a prefix, a router not mounted at all, a second link response schema appearing, the three endpoints drifting onto different database sessions, and the tag filter losing case-sensitivity end to end. - A future endpoint that returns a link should be added to `test_the_three_endpoints_report_a_link_in_one_shape`, so the "one shape" property keeps covering the whole surface.
